raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #47557

Per JSON Schema semantics, a schema without a `type` constraint permits **any** type, and the official OpenAI API behaves that way. vLLM's `extract_types_from_schema()` in `vllm/tool_parsers/utils.py` instead defaulted to `["string"]` whenever no type information could be determined, so a tool parameter whose schema omits `type` (e.g. only has a `description`) always came back as a string — the issue's repro produced `{"value": "5"}` where OpenAI produces `{"value": 5}`.

## Changes

- `extract_types_from_schema()` now returns the full set of JSON types (`string, number, integer, boolean, null, object, array`) when no type info is found, instead of `["string"]`. With the full set, `coerce_to_schema_type()`'s existing priority order (null > integer > number > boolean > object > array > string) coerces values to their natural JSON type: `"5"` → `5`, `"true"` → `true`, `"hello"` → `"hello"`, matching OpenAI behavior.
- `DeepseekV32ToolParser._param_types_for_name()` (the only production caller) now routes its fallback through the same helper, so the streaming path buffers and coerces untyped params exactly like the non-streaming path. No change to `_can_stream_raw_param()` behavior: untyped params were buffered before (string ⊄ {object, array}) and still are.
- Updated the three fallback unit tests and added a `TestUntypedSchemaCoercion` suite covering the issue repro (integer, float, boolean, null, object, array, plain text, and quoted-JSON-string values against an untyped schema).

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

Checked per contribution policy on 2026-07-04:
- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "47557 in:body"` → no results
- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "extract_types_from_schema"` → no results
- Issue #47557 has no linked PRs and no claim comments.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_utils.py -v` (updated + new tests)
- Existing typed-schema tests in the same file guard against regressions (`{"type": "string"}` still returns `["string"]`, enum inference unchanged, etc.).

## Test Result

Development was done on a Windows machine without a vLLM install, so the full pytest suite was not run locally; requesting CI to run it. The changed logic was verified by executing the modified `extract_types_from_schema` + `coerce_to_schema_type` bodies standalone with assertions identical to the updated unit tests (all passed), including the issue repro:

```
coerce_to_schema_type("5", extract_types_from_schema({})) == 5      # was "5"
coerce_to_schema_type("hello", extract_types_from_schema({})) == "hello"
coerce_to_schema_type('"5"', extract_types_from_schema({})) == "5"
extract_types_from_schema({"type": "string"}) == ["string"]         # unchanged
```

         }

+
+
+class TestUntypedSchemaCoercion:
+    """A property schema without a type constraint permits any JSON type,
+    so values should be coerced to their natural JSON type instead of
+    defaulting to string (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47557).
+    """
+
+    def coerce_untyped(self, value: str):
+        return coerce_to_schema_type(value, extract_types_from_schema({}))
+
+    def test_integer_value(self):
+        assert self.coerce_untyped("5") == 5
+
+    def test_float_value(self):
+        assert self.coerce_untyped("3.14") == 3.14
+
+    def test_boolean_value(self):
+        assert self.coerce_untyped("true") is True
+
+    def test_null_value(self):
+        assert self.coerce_untyped("null") is None
+
+    def test_object_value(self):
+        assert self.coerce_untyped('{"a": 1}') == {"a": 1}
+
+    def test_array_value(self):
+        assert self.coerce_untyped("[1, 2]") == [1, 2]
+
+    def test_plain_text_stays_string(self):
+        assert self.coerce_untyped("hello") == "hello"
+
+    def test_numeric_looking_quoted_json_string(self):
+        assert self.coerce_untyped('"5"') == "5"
